destinations.name: Coober Pedy
destinations.coordinates_source: wikipedia:Coober Pedy (town point; re-pin to centre in pin stage)

name_evidence.source: Wikivoyage Coober Pedy; flindersandoutback.com.au/towns/coober-pedy; southaustralia.com Flinders Ranges and Outback
name_evidence.wording: opal-mining town with underground dugouts, the outback's main tourist stop on the Stuart Highway
remote Cooper Creek township, Burke and Wills country, gateway to Innamincka Regional Reserve and Coongie Lakes

spots.bio: Self-guided tour of a mine dug in 1916, with underground homes, in the opal-mining town of Coober Pedy.
spots.name: Old Timers Mine
spots.note: Wikivoyage See listing: self-guided tour of a 1916 mine and underground homes, a signature Coober Pedy visit (rule 2)

spots.bio: Underground opal mine, museum and dugout home showing how Coober Pedy's miners lived and worked.
spots.name: Umoona Opal Mine and Museum
spots.note: southaustralia.com region page names it; underground mine, museum and dugout, a main Coober Pedy attraction (rule 2)

spots.bio: Working opal mine with display seams that visitors tour underground, guided or self-guided.
spots.name: Tom's Working Opal Mine
spots.note: Wikivoyage Coober Pedy calls it 'the pick of the working mines' and Lonely Planet lists it as an attraction (display mine with opal seams, guided or self-guided tours); a place to go underground for an hour, not merely an operator. Objection: one of several Coober Pedy mine visits.

spots.bio: Colourful eroded desert hills called the Breakaways, about 33 km north of Coober Pedy.
spots.name: Kanku-Breakaways Conservation Park
spots.note: 2 counted sources, 1091 page views

spots.bio: Church bored out of solid rock, with a richly ornamented interior.
spots.wiki: Saint Elijah the Prophet Serbian Orthodox Church, Coober Pedy
spots.coordinates_source: wikipedia:Saint Elijah the Prophet Serbian Orthodox Church, Coober Pedy
spots.name: Saint Elijah the Prophet Serbian Orthodox Church
spots.note: Wikivoyage: church bored out of solid rock with a beautifully ornamented interior, a must see (church rule: interior named)

spots.bio: Tour of a hand-dug underground home in Coober Pedy.
spots.name: Faye's Underground Home
spots.note: Wikivoyage Coober Pedy See listing: tour of a hand-dug underground home, open daily except Sunday, $5 (rule 2)

spots.bio: Lunar-like desert plain south of Coober Pedy, used as a film location for Mad Max Beyond Thunderdome and Priscilla.
spots.name: Moon Plain
spots.note: Lonely Planet lists Moon Plain and southaustralia.com's region page names the lunar-like plain and film location (Mad Max Beyond Thunderdome, Priscilla) 15 km from Coober Pedy; a driving/walking sight on the Breakaways loop. Two counted sources.

spots.bio: Giant winch that doubles as a lookout over the Coober Pedy opal fields.
spots.name: Big Winch
spots.note: Wikivoyage See listing: lookout in the middle of Coober Pedy over the opal fields; a landmark Big Thing (rule 2,3)

spots.bio: Grassless desert golf course 3 km from Coober Pedy, where players carry a piece of turf to tee off.
spots.name: Coober Pedy Golf Club
spots.note: Wikivoyage names the grassless desert course (players carry a piece of turf to tee off) as a quirky thing to do 3 km from Coober Pedy; an open public course visitors play, a recognised quirky icon.

spots.bio: Reserve of 1.3 million hectares along Cooper Creek, with waterholes for fishing and canoeing.
spots.name: Innamincka Regional Reserve
spots.note: parks.sa.gov.au visitor page: 1.3 million ha reserve with Cooper Creek waterholes for fishing and canoeing, Cullyamurra Waterhole, the visitor centre and Burke and Wills sites; Flinders & Outback also names it. Objection: parts closed in floods and it overlaps Cullyamurra.

spots.bio: Australia's largest billabong on Cooper Creek, a canoeing and paddling spot significant to the Traditional Owners.
spots.name: Cullyamurra Waterhole
spots.note: Rule 1+2: Flinders & Outback (opened) names Australia's largest billabong as a canoe/paddle destination on Cooper Creek, significant to the Traditional Owners.

spots.bio: Arid-zone wetland of lakes and channels, reached by 4WD, for birdlife and canoeing.
spots.name: Malkumba–Coongie Lakes National Park
spots.note: Rule 1+2: Flinders & Outback park page (opened) calls it one of SA's most spectacular natural attractions: arid wetland, birds, canoeing; 4WD access. Keeps the Coongie Lakes duplicate as this one.

spots.bio: Heritage-listed former Inland Mission building, now Innamincka's park headquarters with Burke and Wills displays.
spots.name: Elizabeth Symon Nursing Home
spots.note: Wikivoyage Innamincka See lists it, and the parks.sa.gov.au page says the heritage-listed park headquarters and interpretation centre (the former Australian Inland Mission building, i.e. the nursing home) is always open in the town centre, with natural history and Burke and Wills displays. Objection: more an information centre than a sight.

spots.bio: 617 km outback track from Marree to Marla, past old railway sidings, mound springs and Lake Eyre South.
spots.name: Oodnadatta Track
spots.note: Wikivoyage itinerary page gives the 617 km track its own article with sidings, mound springs and Lake Eyre South; an obvious outback draw (rule 1)

spots.bio: Long outback track from Marree to Birdsville across the Tirari Desert, with the Mungerannie Hotel halfway.
spots.name: Birdsville Track
spots.note: 2 counted sources, 9529 page views

spots.bio: Australia's largest salt lake and the national park around it.
spots.name: Kati Thanda–Lake Eyre National Park
spots.note: 2 counted sources, 2021 page views

spots.bio: Australia's largest national park, a 4WD desert of red dunes that needs a Desert Parks Pass.
spots.name: Munga-Thirri–Simpson Desert National Park
spots.note: Rule 1+2: Flinders & Outback national-parks page (opened) presents the Simpson Desert dunes as a headline 4WD destination; Desert Parks Pass, closed 1 Dec-15 Mar (note season).

spots.bio: Remote north-western park with Dalhousie Springs and camping at Mount Dare.
spots.name: Witjira National Park
spots.note: Rule 1+2: Flinders & Outback outback page (opened) features Dalhousie Springs (swim in 37C artesian springs) and Mount Dare camping in Witjira.

spots.bio: Largest artesian spring complex in the area, with 37C water to swim in, inside Witjira National Park.
spots.name: Dalhousie Springs
spots.note: 2 counted sources, 3117 page views

spots.bio: The two best-known mound springs on the Oodnadatta Track, near Coward Springs.
spots.wiki: Wabma Kadarbu Mound Springs Conservation Park
spots.name: The Bubbler and Blanche Cup
spots.note: Wikivoyage Oodnadatta Track: the two best-known mound springs, a worthwhile diversion (rule 1,2)

spots.bio: Historic railway siding on the Oodnadatta Track with a date-palm spa, a self-guided walk and camel safaris.
spots.name: Coward Springs
spots.note: Rule 1+2: Wikivoyage (Oodnadatta Track) names the spa, historic rail siding, self-guided walk and camel safari; a second-tier Oodnadatta Track stop with things to do (opened).

spots.bio: Preserved Ghan railway siding on the Oodnadatta Track that shows how railway settlers lived.
spots.name: Curdimurka Siding
spots.note: Wikivoyage: preserved Ghan siding showing how settlers lived, one of the interesting sidings on the track (rule 2)

spots.bio: Historic railway bridge on the Oodnadatta Track, the longest bridge in South Australia.
spots.name: Algebuckina Bridge
spots.note: Rule 1+3: Wikivoyage Oodnadatta Track singles out the longest bridge in South Australia as a sight (opened); a named heritage roadside stop.

spots.bio: Tiny Oodnadatta Track settlement with a famously remote pub, the base for Lake Eyre scenic flights.
spots.name: William Creek
spots.note: Town with its own Wikivoyage page and flindersandoutback.com.au town page; the William Creek Hotel pub is a named stop on the Oodnadatta Track (rule 1, 2)

spots.bio: Pink roadhouse at Oodnadatta, the Oodnadatta Track's information hub.
spots.name: Pink Roadhouse
spots.note: Rule 3 'quirky roadside icon': Wikivoyage Oodnadatta and Flinders & Outback both name the pink roadhouse as a feature of the town and the track's information hub (opened).

spots.bio: Museum in Oodnadatta's preserved old Ghan railway station.
spots.name: Railway Tjukurpa Museum
spots.note: Rule 1+2: Wikivoyage Oodnadatta lists the preserved Ghan station museum, open daily 9-5 (opened).

spots.bio: Outback railway town at the start of the Birdsville and Oodnadatta Tracks.
spots.name: Marree
spots.note: 2 counted sources, 14608 page views

spots.bio: Recreation of Australia's first mosque, built by Afghan cameleers.
spots.name: Marree Mosque
spots.note: Wikivoyage See listing: recreation of Australia's first mosque built by Afghan cameleers (rule 2)

spots.bio: Outback pub and roadhouse halfway along the Birdsville Track, known for its memorabilia.
spots.name: Mungerannie
spots.note: Mungerannie Hotel is named by Flinders & Outback as acclaimed for its outback memorabilia (hats, locks of hair), a quirky roadside icon halfway along the Birdsville Track; second-tier quirky stop the bar keeps.

spots.bio: Opal-mining village near Roxby Downs where visitors can noodle for opal.
spots.name: Andamooka
spots.note: 2 counted sources, 14497 page views

spots.bio: Fenced arid-zone reserve near Roxby Downs where rare desert species are seen on tours.
spots.name: Roxby Downs Arid Recovery Reserve
spots.note: Flinders & Outback names Arid Recovery in both the region page and the Roxby Downs town page (sunset tag-along tours, spotlight walks, Roxby Discovery Tour) to see rare arid-zone species in a fenced reserve; visits are by tour only. Objection: access only via tours.

spots.bio: Free open-air display of missiles, rockets and aircraft in the centre of Woomera.
spots.name: Woomera Missile Park
spots.note: Wikivoyage See listing: free open-air display of missiles and rockets in the town centre, with the Heritage Centre beside it (rule 2)

spots.bio: Rocket Range museum in the Woomera visitor centre.
spots.name: Woomera Heritage Centre
spots.note: Wikivoyage lists the Rocket Range Museum in the visitors' centre, about an hour, $6 (rule 2)

spots.bio: Pink salt lake beside the Stuart Highway south of Glendambo.
spots.name: Lake Hart
spots.note: southaustralia.com region page names the pink salt lake beside the Stuart Highway; a roadside stop travellers photograph

review.name: Painted Desert (South Australia)
review.reason: For: Wikivoyage names it, SA Heritage lists the Arckaringa Hills state heritage area, and Arckaringa Station offers a walk (~1.5 km) and lookout at sunset; distinct natural sight. Against: only one counted source (Wikivoyage Stuart Highway, 'all-wheel track'), sits on a private pastoral lease with restricted, fragile access, 120-150 km from Coober Pedy; no tourism-board page found.

review.name: Catholic Catacomb Church
review.reason: For: Wikivoyage Coober Pedy calls the underground Catholic church 'a significant site' and Coober Pedy's carved-rock churches are a signature visit. Against: Wikivoyage ranks it less intricate than the Serbian Orthodox church; one counted source; the candidate's wiki title (Catacomb Church) is actually the Anglican church, so name and article conflict and the Catholic church's identity needs checking.

review.name: Marree Man
review.reason: For: Wikivoyage Marree See entry and Flinders & Outback both name it; a famous 4.2 km geoglyph. Against: it cannot be seen from the ground and the experience is a charter flight from Marree (an operator), so a visitor 'goes' to nothing; only the flight reaches it.

review.name: Kalamurina Sanctuary
review.reason: For: AWC (the manager) describes a 679,000 ha wildlife sanctuary on the Warburton River with an interpretive walk on Outback Spirit pre-booked tours (April-October). Against: no tourism-board or guide source; third-party listings say camping is closed and entry is tours only, and AWC's own page allows booked self-drive at $40 per vehicle, so access sources conflict.
